findings.claim: Official test set = 5,344 JPEG crops (IDs 0-14,806 with gaps), all ~291-300 px tall, widths 445-1,630 (mean 902) on a 70-image sample: word/line crops, not pages.
ID bucket distribution is uneven: 0-999=56, 1000-1999=481, 10000-14000 four full buckets of 1,000, 14000-14806=807. Test IDs are sparse in the low range (possible hint of different source batches).

Tesseract (eng/hin/kan/mal/tam/tel) on 70 stratified test images: 55.7% UNKNOWN, Devanagari 35.7%, Latin 4.3%, Tamil 1.4%, Kannada 1.4%, Other 1.4%. Script-id by Tesseract is unreliable on handwriting; the 35.7% Devanagari is likely misread Bengali (shared headline)
Planner viewed 3 test images (10001, 12407, 1361): each one handwritten word in Bengali script, blue pen, ~300 px tall. Only 3 images viewed directly in this doc.
Only labelled handwriting set on disk is Datasets/akshardrishti_official/Bodo/gu (Gujarati handwritten words, IIIT-HW format): train 82,563 / val 17,643 / test 16,490 lines, vocab 10,963 words.

DATA-INTEGRITY: Bodo/gu label files list 82,563 train entries but only 4,645 image files exist on disk (~77,918 missing, ~5%). Training would silently use 5% of labels; must be verified against source (IIIT-HW-Dev/-Telugu/-INDIC-HW-WORDS). Note folder named Bodo but script Gujarati.

No other handwriting set found in akshardrishti_official; South-language folders (Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam) are PDFs only (0/23,001 clean pages, proto-104 S1), no handwriting labels. No Bengali HW labelled data on disk at all.
